description.narrative:
The proposed project introduces community-based innovative flood protection measures that leverage local resources and knowledge toeffectively manage flood risks. The solutions include last-mile early warning information dissemination based on predetermined triggers and reforestation/afforestation for riverbank protection against floods in selected hotspots. This is coupled with the eco-hydrological benefits of riverbank reforestation using indigenous, drought-resistant trees, which enhance soil stability and water infiltration, thereby reducing flood risks in a sustainable manner. The combined effect of timely warnings and nature-based defenses creates a synergistic approach to flood resilience.
The proposed solutions aim to fulfill the following broad anticipatory action objective in addition to a resilience objective: 1. Enhance access to early warning information: Increase households' and communities' access to timely and actionable early warning information, empowering them to make informed decisions related to flood risk management. Currently early warning messages are only disseminated through mobile phone text messages. However, gaps remain in the last mile communities. We aim to work with these communities to see how we can best ensure messaging will also reach them in the future. In thepilot we will test ways to reach these communities and form recommendations for a more inclusive early warning system in different parts of Somalia. 2. Safeguard lives and assets before floods take place and reduce its impact on communities: Enable supported households to protect their lives, as well as their household and livelihood assets, from the impact of flooding through afforestation/reforestation of the riverbanks.
The proposed approach aligns well with the principles of integrated flood risk management (IFRM). It integrates non-structural measures like early warning systems with nature-based structural measures (reforestation). This strategyaddresses both the probability and the consequences of flooding, moving beyond traditional reliance on purely structural or technological solutions, which often face limitations as documented WFP in Somalia
This proposed project also aims to address the immediate flood protection needs of the most vulnerable groups, including women, girls, boys, elderly people, and individuals with special needs who are expected to be affected by the floods. The primary users of this solution are all households in the two villages of Halgan and Bayahow, where two weak riverbanks are located. These riverbanks are well-known for their susceptibility to flooding.
The indirect beneficiaries of this project will be diverse communities, with households from various provinces, districts, and villages participating. The project will benefit a broad representation of households, including displaced and non-displaced individuals across the Jowhar District of the Middle Shabelle Region.
For this project, SAACID will maintain close coordination with Oxfam as the lead INGO for SOMJR project in South-Central Somalia. This partnership will also collaborate actively with the affected community, continue with close collaboration with the local authority, and relevant Clusters and government line ministries.

participating-org.narrative:
SAACID is an indigenous Somali not-for-profit, non-political, non-governmental organization founded and directed by Somali women that focuses on practical measures to enhance life-options of women, children and the poor. SAACID was originally founded in Somalia on October 3rd 1990, and is one of the Somalia’s oldest continuously operational indigenous non-governmental women organization. SAACID has continually operated in the anarchic context of Somalia for more than 32 years now.
This organization has been dedicated to the empowerment of Somali women, children and the poor. SAACID has earned reputation among their local and international partners for the heist quality of work – for accountability, sustainability, responsibility, and sensitivity. SAACID is full member of Core Humanitarian Standards known as CHS Alliance.
SAACID Mission is To help women, children and the poor achieve their full human potential SAACID Vision is A world in which all women, children, and the poor have full equality and full access to the resources necessary to fulfill their human potential
Focal areas: SAACID has developed enormous operational experience in operating in an anarchic context; and has garnered very significant trust and legitimacy from all clan structures in Somalia. SAACID has worked in 7 operational sectors in its operational history: 1. Women’s Empowerment 2. Education 3. Health, Nutrition, Water and Sanitation 4. Development and Livelihoods 5. Conflict Resolution and Governance 6. Emergency Relief 7. Research
SAACID Services include: Project implementation, Health, Nutrition, Food Security <(>&<)> Livelihood, WASH, Consultancy, Research, Baseline and feasibility studies.
Clients include : UN Agencies, International donors, Medair, Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), local private sector, academia and civil society partners.
